item.title: Sea level much higher than assumed in most coastal hazard assessments
item.description:
📝 Here we show that more than 99% of the evaluated impact assessments handled sea-level and land elevation data inadequately, thereby misjudging sea level relative to coastal elevation. Consequently, the impacts of RSLR and coastal (and compound) flooding are closely related to coastal elevation relative to sea level. Apart from considering vertical uncertainty of elevation data, using DEMs in coastal hazard assessments requires correctly combining coastal elevation with local sea-level height and the proper conversion to a common vertical reference frame2,3.
🔗 Read more: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10196-1
